lead: Pittsburgh plumbing deals with steep hills, very old homes, lead lines and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Pittsburgh.
risk: lead and galvanized service lines, failing sewer laterals on steep lots and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, sewer laterals and frozen pipes
why: Pittsburgh has one of the oldest housing stocks in the country. Lawrenceville, Bloomfield and the South Side have row houses and frame homes with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and long sewer laterals down steep lots.
Heavy rain overloads the combined sewers and backs water into basements. Winters freeze pipes in exterior walls and unheated spaces.
water: Pittsburgh Water draws from the Allegheny River. The water is moderately hard. The utility has replaced thousands of lead service lines and has an address lookup.
tips: Check Pittsburgh Water's lead line lookup.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Scope the sewer lateral before buying.
areas: PipeMend works in Lawrenceville, Shadyside, Squirrel Hill, Mount Washington, the Strip District, Bloomfield and every other Pittsburgh neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits and plumber licenses in Pittsburgh come from the Allegheny County Health Department's plumbing program.

faq.a: Pennsylvania has no state plumber license. In Pittsburgh and the rest of Allegheny County, the county Health Department licenses plumbers and issues plumbing permits.
